speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; the combination of night sweats, significant weight loss, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy raises suspicion for malignancy or chronic infection. To help narrow this down, do you have a history of smoking or alcohol use, and have you noticed any skin changes like jaundice or bruising? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count with differential. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_US.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (likely Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma or Hodgkin Lymphoma).

The combination of constitutional symptoms (B-symptoms), supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and cytopenias on blood work strongly suggests a malignancy of the lymphatic system. Given the abdominal involvement and organomegaly, staging with a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis is the next critical step.
